- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-1.0), model underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use lagged 3–5 day average as ceiling.
- If model forecast is significantly below recent 10-day moving average, consider upward bias correction — especially if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overpredicts late-period (last 7–10 days) prices; apply downward bias to final 5–7 days if sentiment is weak or mixed.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-period, model often fails to catch momentum; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% per sentiment shift.
- Avoid overreacting to single-day sentiment spikes — model often overcorrects; use 3-day rolling sentiment average for smoothing.
